city.name: Shinagawa
city.description: Shinagawa and Takanawa from open data, lit by the real sun: the station between the Takanawa hills and Konan's towers, Takanawa Gateway's folded roof, and the old Tokaido's first post town at Kita-Shinagawa.

tour.title: Shinagawa, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's 5 m laser-scanned bare earth.

tour.title: Takanawa Gateway
tour.text: The Yamanote line's newest station, 2020, its roof folded like paper, on the rail yard that is becoming a new quarter.

tour.title: Shinagawa-shuku
tour.text: The old Tokaido's first post town south of the Yatsuyama bridge, its shops and lanterns. The signs here are typical of the street, not its real shops'.

minor_labels: グランドプリンスホテル新高輪

shore.encoding: r: 128 + 2 x signed distance to the shoreline (m, water positive); g: sand; b: rock

seawall.note: The rivers' and the bay's revetments and the castle moats: granite blocks and concrete.

trees.note: Species are not mapped, and the shared trees have no ginkgo or cherry, so the mix stands in: elms for the zelkovas, plane trees for the street planes and ginkgos. A guess, not a survey.

sources.heights: MLIT Project PLATEAU Tokyo 23 wards LOD2 building models (CC BY 4.0), as vector tiles by indigo-lab (MIT)
sources.buildings: Overture Maps Foundation, release 2026-10-21.0 (OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; Microsoft ML Buildings, ODbL)
sources.terrain: GSI Fundamental Geospatial Data DEM5A, 5 m airborne laser survey bare earth (GSI terms of use); 10 m DEM where 5A is absent
sources.imagery: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) seamless aerial photographs (GSI terms of use, source attribution)
sources.trees: Overture base land, tree points and rows (OpenStreetMap, ODbL); heights not mapped
sources.landmarks: Takanawa Gateway Station (Kengo Kuma, 2020; East Japan Railway Company) on OpenStreetMap's footprint, its folded roof from photographs; the old Tokaido on OpenStreetMap's line. The post town's signs are indicative: typical trades, no real shops' signs.
sources.fonts: Signs drawn with Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License: Zen Kaku Gothic New, Shippori Mincho
sources.canopy: Meta and World Resources Institute High Resolution Canopy Height Maps (Tolan et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0): trees planted from the canopy in mapped woods and parks

woods.encoding: r: ground cover under the canopy (0-255), g: canopy height x 8 (m), b: a footway under the canopy, a: in a wood or park
woods.source: Meta and World Resources Institute High Resolution Canopy Height Maps (Tolan et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0): trees planted from the canopy in mapped woods and parks
